newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo spars with left as Mexico election heats up.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo spars with left as Mexico election heats up.

text.p: President Ernesto Zedillo sharply attacked the leader of Mexico's main leftist party in a letter published on Thursday as the country's election campaign heated up.
Mexico faces crucial congressional and gubernatorial votes in July that could rob the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) of its majority in the lower house for the first time ever.
Zedillo has proclaimed a commitment to greater democracy and a more level electoral playing field in a country dominated by his party for the last 68 years.

But opposition parties have complained bitterly in recent weeks that the president appears to have jettisoned that promise and thrown his full weight behind securing yet another PRI victory, by fair means or foul.

Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, leader of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) complained in two letters to Zedillo that the president had turned himself into a "PRI campaign chief" and was backing a dirty smear campaign against the opposition.
Zedillo shot back on Thursday, defending his right to campaign for the PRI and speak out.
"Neither the law nor democracy entitles you to ask me to keep silent about the political propaganda of your party, which is based on reviling the government," Zedillo said.

The slinging match was triggered by Zedillo's appearance at a PRI convention April 12 to salute the party's candidates. At the event, Zedillo told the PRI candidates that he needed them to win the election to guarantee the continuity of his programme.
Opposition parties and political analysts seized on his remarks as proof that the president had abandoned his commitment to opening up Mexico's political system.

Lopez Obrador, whose PRD party is third placed nationally but the favourite to win the Mexico City mayor's election, was particularly upset about the arrest of Alfredo Lopez Ramos, a PRD congressional candidates in the southern state of Oaxaca.
In his second letter to Zedillo, the PRD chief said he had a tape recording of the PRI party boss in Oaxaca threatening Lopez Ramos unless he withdrew his candidacy.
"The next day, on registering as a candidate, he (Lopez Ramos) received an arrest warrant and 24 hours later he was jailed," Lopez Obrador said.
Zedillo did not mention the Oaxaca arrest by name in his reply but urged the PRD to make a formal complaint through the correct legal channels if it had any proof of illegal acts.
"Democratic change in Mexico is not now a distant project of some, it is now a reality for all," Zedillo insisted.
